content:
UPDATE (21st November 2026): Did anyone else see odd lights in the sky (compass heading North 0-10 degrees, roughly) on Thursday 19th November 2026 between 1am and 2am UK time? I'm southwest of Gatwick Airport. Spotlights moving in various ways across the sky, explosions or bursts of white light, balls of cloud-like light racing across the sky from all directions (side to side, etc), all different sizes.

They looked similar to the lights in the below video, but the ones I saw varied so much in size and behaviour:
https://www.facebook.com/reel/336646404842796

I have spoken with a number of official, relevant agencies: the Met Office, MoD police, a nearby UCL space lab/observatory (where the professor who could have discussed the sighting with me is now retired, and no one else there knows enough about it to give me an answer), the Geomagnetism team over at the British Geological Survey... The overall consensus is that it could not have been aurora borealis (northern lights), as the conditions were nowhere near right at the time, plus no record of such a geomagnetic event occurring at that time. My description of what I witnessed matches no one's experience or knowledge of northern lights. The closest suggestion of an "answer" from British Geological Survey is lightning, which may have caused the "bursts" of light, but no reply about the synchronous manoeuvres; I guess ball lightning is not a possibility, as they would have mentioned it.

I am checking with local venues and even farther out re: potential testing of laser or light displays, though so far it seems none were operating at that time.

I've logged a report with the non-emergency police, too, in case of drone activity.

Additionally, there are two other local people who viewed the lights.

REMINDER OF MY ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION: Suspected it might be aurora borealis (northern lights), which I have never been in person for, but some aspects don't match up. At one point three balls of cloud-like light were spinning in unison; I'm given to understand that aurora borealis cannot achieve this or has never been observed doing so. I viewed none of the colours (green, purple, red, et al) associated with an aurora borealis; the white lights seemed independent of anything else in the sky.
